data.hook: Ricursive releases Ripple-65B Preview, an open-weight model it says leads on a coding benchmark.
data.outro: Full sources for every story are linked on our website.

stories.headline: Ricursive releases Ripple-65B Preview open-weight model, citing TerminalBench lead
stories.summary: Ricursive Intelligence released Ripple-65B Preview, a general-purpose variant of the proprietary model behind its AI chip design platform. The company says the dense Transformer was pretrained on 12 trillion tokens, supports up to 1M context, and scored 80.52 on TerminalBench 2.1. The model is available on Hugging Face, Together AI, GMI Cloud, OpenRouter and Fireworks.
stories.why_it_matters: Developers building agentic coding tools gain another open-weight option, which the company says can also run on local devices such as NVIDIA DGX Spark.
stories.limitations: The benchmark and cost figures are the company's own and have not been independently confirmed in the verified sources.
stories.card_text: Ripple-65B Preview: open-weight model, company says 80.52 on TerminalBench 2.1
stories.narration: Ricursive Intelligence released Ripple-65B Preview, an open-weight model available on Hugging Face and several cloud providers. The company says it scores eighty point five two on TerminalBench two point one, and that it cost 32 million dollars to develop.

stories.headline: ReTrace turns agent runs into fixed workflows, trading some accuracy for speed and cost
stories.summary: Researchers present ReTrace, a method that builds a reusable workflow from an SOP and a few logged agent runs, so code rather than an LLM selects each next step. The authors report 93.8% completion on 79 procedures versus 96.8% for the agent, at 24% lower cost per task. On τ²-Bench, they report 75.8% task success versus 80.6% for the agent, with runs taking 1.3 seconds instead of 170.
stories.why_it_matters: Teams running LLM agents at scale, where a model call for every step adds latency and cost, could cut both if workflows hold up on their tasks.
stories.limitations: The results are the authors' own benchmarks, including figures from their production platform, and the accuracy gap to the agent remains.
stories.card_text: ReTrace: code picks agent steps, authors report 24% lower cost per task
stories.narration: A new arXiv paper describes ReTrace, which turns agent runs into fixed workflows where code, not a language model, chooses each step. The authors say it cuts cost per task by twenty-four percent, though completion trails the agent.

stories.headline: Hugging Face releases LeRobot v0.7.0 with streamed training data and new robot models
stories.summary: Hugging Face released LeRobot v0.7.0, which adds interactive rollouts and lets users train on datasets streamed from the Hub, a Storage Bucket or LanceDB without downloading them first. The release adds four world action models and four new VLAs. The company says streaming gives 2.1 to 2.5 times more samples per second with four DataLoader workers.
stories.why_it_matters: Robotics researchers and developers working with large Physical AI datasets can train without full downloads, which the company says speeds up training.
stories.limitations: G0.5 is released under a non-commercial community license rather than Apache-2.0, and the speed figures are Hugging Face's own measurements.
stories.card_text: LeRobot v0.7.0: stream training data straight from the Hub, no downloads
stories.narration: Hugging Face released LeRobot version zero point seven, letting robotics teams train on streamed data without downloads. The company says streaming runs two to two and a half times faster.

stories.headline: NVIDIA, Rebellions and SK Telecom partner on Korean sovereign AI infrastructure
stories.summary: NVIDIA, Rebellions and SK Telecom announced a collaboration to advance Korea's sovereign AI infrastructure using NVIDIA NVLink Fusion. Rebellions will connect its Rebel R200 NPUs to the NVIDIA platform using the MGX rack architecture, and SK Telecom plans to deploy the systems in its AI data center. The companies plan disaggregated inference, with NVIDIA GPUs for prefill and Rebellions NPUs for decode.
stories.why_it_matters: Korean AI operators and chipmakers gain a path to combine domestic NPUs with NVIDIA systems, which the companies say may improve inference throughput and power efficiency.
stories.limitations: Rebellions expects R200 systems to be ready for deployment in 2028, so the planned throughput and efficiency gains are not yet demonstrated.
stories.card_text: R200 systems expected ready in 2028 for Korea sovereign AI, companies say
stories.narration: NVIDIA, Rebellions and SK Telecom announced a collaboration on Korea's sovereign AI infrastructure. Rebellions' R200 systems are expected to be ready for deployment in 2028, the companies say.

stories.headline: UK government backs chip startup Fractile in funding round worth over £500 million
stories.summary: The UK Government's Sovereign AI Venture Fund and the British Business Bank have backed Fractile, a London and Bristol-based AI chip startup. The Series C round is worth over £500 million and values the company at over £5 billion, according to the government. Investors CapitalG, Lightspeed and Redpoint also participate, and the government's specific investment amounts are not disclosed.
stories.why_it_matters: The government says the investment will reduce reliance on overseas technology and strengthen UK capabilities in critical technologies.
stories.limitations: Government investment amounts are undisclosed, and the claims that Fractile's chips are faster and less costly come from the government's description.
stories.card_text: UK backs AI chip startup Fractile in £500m+ Series C at £5bn+ valuation
stories.narration: The UK government and British Business Bank have backed Fractile, a British AI chip startup, in a Series C round worth over five hundred million pounds. The government says the round values Fractile at over five billion pounds.
